newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein lower on eve of polls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein lower on eve of polls.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were lower in late trading on Wednesday as cautious buyers stayed sidelined ahead of Thursday's general election, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,400 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,400-05 rupiah at the opening. Crude palm oil was done at 1,240 rupiah/kg and 1,243 rupiah/kg at a tender for two parcels of 500 tonnes each in Medan.

"The tender price seems to be on the high side considering current palm olein prices," one trader said. "The market was mostly quiet ahead of the elections. Many players will be closed tomorrow in case there is any election-related violence."

Nearly 125 million Indonesians are eligible to vote in Thursday's five-yearly election which has been marred by the worst political violence in more than three decades. The Japanese embassy in Jakarta was evacuated early on Wednesday after an unidentified telephone caller made a bomb threat.
A shopping complex in the North Sumatran capital of Medan was also evacuated after a similar call. In both instances, the threats turned out to be hoaxes.
"Although there was no bomb found at the Medan Plaza, people are still afraid," one trader from the key producing area said. "I will be closed tomorrow because of the elections."
The traders said players who were opened for business on Thursday in Jakarta were not expected to deliver oil to their customers as a precaution against possible street protests.
"I have informed my clients to come and get their oil today or after the elections," one trader said. "Anyway the market is expected to be very quiet tomorrow."
The traders said they expected the market, which has been subdued during most of the 27-day campaign period that ended last Friday, to return to normal in early June.
